grades.quote: Legal Counsel will review the Report and the written notice from the Responsible Officer and initiate one of the following processes:
The University will maintain a website that includes information about Sexualized Violence, Consent, Disclosures and Reporting.

Victims/Survivors who wish to Report Sexualized Violence to the University can be supported in doing so by the Sexualized Violence Prevention and Response Manager. Reports will be directed to the appropriate Responsible Officer.
Either the Complainant or the Respondent may request that the investigator ask questions of the other or any person related to the evidence.
Victims/Survivors need only disclose their experience to seek support and will not be required or pressured to make a formal Report to University authorities or the police.
The investigator will endeavor to complete the investigation within 60 days of being appointed.
To protect the integrity of the Investigation, the University will normally issue a no-contact order to both the Complainant and the Respondent.

A Student includes any of the following: an undergraduate who is enrolled at the University for one or more of the last two terms (including in a practicum placement, cooperative education or study abroad) and is eligible to continue in a program of study;
the sanction imposed against the Respondent, which will be redacted from the letter to the Complainant unless knowledge of the sanction is necessary to protect the Complainant’s health or safety.
The President will report annually to the Board on progress with implementing this policy
Mandatory training will be provided to all faculty, staff and administrators on the fundamentals of receiving a disclosure and providing supports.
Sexualized Violence information and education will be provided to new incoming Students and Employees each semester through either online or in-person orientation programming.
